title: Large personal CPC, Amiga and DOS application/restoration discovery
summary: Personally screen 234 candidate URLs and add 17 projects, with five explicit non-promotion decisions.
notes: Root assistant personally searched 20 routes, reviewed 22 candidate repositories and inspected implementation and build material. This pass adds 17 game/application/early-system restorations plus 5 explicit scope or implementation decisions. CPC Oh Mummy uses reconstructed code and separate assets; stale source-header prose is distinguished from current directives. DOS applications include QuickCD and 486TEST, and Amiga Banker is original-author source preservation. CPU-emulated browser reconstructions, source-unavailable narratives and modern tools are not presented as native historical engine recovery. Unpacked-reference matching, lifted runtime/data, and functional rather than byte-exact equivalence are explicit. No candidate program, hardware test, installer or game was executed.

sources.reason: Modernizes recovered v451.03 Desert Storm code with SDL3, higher resolution, sound and input fixes; retains a separate 32-bit DOS preview.
Collection preserves reconstructed 86-DOS/PC-DOS kernel assembly snapshots, with period interfaces and revision history visible in source.
Builds period Paterson kernel source with newly authored boot sector and BIOS layer implementing historical register-level contracts.
Recovers actor/game systems with original segment-offset annotations and differential/proof tooling, then links them with lifted runtime/data segments.
Recreates DOS MSCDEX audio control and Win16 MCI dialog paths, with hybrid executable packaging and supporting DLL source.
Routine-by-routine C++ port preserves recovered game/data layout and original-address commentary while SDL3 supplies host interfaces.
Native Rust code recovers management rules and original-format images, audio, club data and encrypted saves from addressed DOS executable analysis.
Author Cédric Beust publishes original 1990s bank-account application sources, including recurring-entry logic, database, UI and localization.
Reconstructs MUMMY1 engine and detokenized BASIC loader with firmware symbols, named game/data routines and extracted sprite/tile resources.
Unpacks and annotates BASIC-PDS executable, exposes x87 stress kernel and emits NASM source preserving MZ layout and encodings.
Collects reconstructed COMMAND, CHKDSK, FORMAT, SYS and kernel-related components across 86-DOS/MS-DOS/PC-DOS 1.x.
Reconstructs RAIDER.EXE code with actor structures and named routines plus separate assembly graphics data segments.
Restores game/editor/setup/library source using released 1.35 material and 1.40 executable disassembly, preserving DOS-focused program structure.
Michael Steil’s named NASM boot-sector and IBMBIO listings explain early PC-DOS disk, keyboard and hardware interfaces.
Native subsystem-oriented C reconstructs character control, collision, levels and overlays with original address mapping and headless state/replay API.
Translates DOS Robbo C/C++ grid logic and interaction tables to Lua, with original tick ordering and adapted monochrome viewport/control presentation.
Recovers game-owned functions, named data and resource/level knowledge with versioned Ghidra analysis; retains assembly hardware routines and separately reconstructed audio library.
Modern Electron disk-image tool, not restored historical Amiga Imagine application. Relevant tooling can be reviewed separately; no game/application reconstruction established.

Detailed CPC reverse-engineering narrative and images, but no textual implementation/disassembly source found in the inspected tree. Retain as a lead pending availability/review of source rather than imply buildable reconstruction.

Original Z80 game executes inside JavaScript CPC emulator with a WebGL rendering replacement. Extraction research exists, but retain game-specific emulation audit rather than promote browser product as native engine reconstruction.

Inspected asm2c runtime explicitly models 8086 registers, flags, memory and interrupt handling for generated game programs. Retain architecture audit; unlike SDLPoP2, this is not established as a native high-level subsystem reconstruction.
Historical DOS virus disassembly, not a game/application restoration within this focused request. Only identity/README screened; no malware code executed or modified.
